conventions.convention: The pointwise algebraic estimates use m,c>0, 0<δ<1, |v|/c≤δ, z=|v|²/c², γ=(1−z)^(−1/2), p=mγv and E=γmc². Zero velocity is included.
Uniform low-speed families satisfy |v|≤C√ε c, 0<ε≤ε*, and ρ=C²ε*<1. The rest-adjusted coordinate-time density is L_c+mc², where L_c=−mc²√(1−|v|²/c²).

The Euclidean ODE comparison assumes existing C¹ solutions on [0,T], common compact convex containment, a state-Lipschitz bound for F_0, and a uniform field-error bound. Bounded field values alone do not establish stability or existence.
The Lorentzian signature is (−,+,+,+). Observers have g(n,n)=−1; proper-time massive tangents have g(U,U)=−c². Massive worldlines are C² future-timelike curves on open parameter intervals.

Shell continuation is relative to an open coordinate-state domain D⊆R⁸. Compact containment means containment in a compact subset of D; finite maximal endpoints eventually leave every such compact subset.
The EM comparison uses time-first fields E(t,x)=E_s(x,t), B(t,x)=B_s(x,t), and the dimensionless block norm |x|/L*+|p|/P*. Its Lipschitz constant and field-error estimate use this same norm.

The EM limit holds prescribed fields, m and q fixed while the formal model parameter c tends to infinity. It assumes common-interval solutions and containment; it imposes no Maxwell equations and reports no empirical variation of c.

Flat inertial kinematic reduction and curved weak-field geodesic reduction are separate branches. The curved branch retains exactly GR hypotheses (H1)–(H3), uses a fixed scaled interval [0,S*], and has coordinate-time horizon LS*/(√ε c).

load_bearing.statement: For the smooth autonomous coordinate shell-force field on an open domain D⊆R⁸ and normalized future-timelike initial data, compact containment near either finite endpoint of the unique maximal solution permits extension past that endpoint. More strongly, at each finite maximal endpoint the solution eventually leaves every compact subset of D.

For C>0, ε*>0, ρ=C²ε*<1, 0<ε≤ε*, m,c>0 and |v|≤C√ε c, the pointwise gamma, momentum and energy bounds hold uniformly with z≤ρ; additionally |L_c(v)+mc²−L_N(v)|≤mC⁴c²ε²/[8(1−ρ)^(3/2)], where L_c=−mc²√(1−|v|²/c²) and L_N=m|v|²/2.

Under the stated continuous-field, boundedness, compact convex containment, F_0 state-Lipschitz bound L and uniform field-error bound η, existing C¹ solutions on [0,T] satisfy ||z_ε(t)−z_0(t)||₂≤(||z_ε(0)−z_0(0)||₂+ηt)e^(Lt). Equal initial states give supremum error at most ηTe^(LT).
